cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: The GET handler resolves the document straight from the id in the URL and returns its body, but never checks that the signed-in user holds a membership in document.workspaceId - the PATCH handler further down the same file does exactly that check. Any authenticated user of any tenant can read any document by guessing or leaking its id.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: The q, sort and dir query parameters are concatenated into the statement template and executed with prisma.$queryRawUnsafe. q is placed inside single-quoted SQL literals, so a quote closes them, and sort and dir are dropped into the ORDER BY clause where there is no quoting at all - the membership check above only constrains which workspace the intended query reads.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: Also hand-written SQL over the same tables, but it runs through prisma.$queryRaw with a Prisma.sql tagged template, so the workspace id and the date window are bound as query parameters; the one client-chosen fragment, the sort order, is selected from a fixed map of pre-built Prisma.sql values and the row limit is clamped to a number.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: The handler selects expiresAt and revokedAt on the shareLink row and then never reads either value before returning the document body to an unauthenticated caller, so a link the owner revoked and a link past its expiry date both keep serving content until a nightly prune job happens to delete the row.

cases.why: The same unauthenticated capability-token lookup against the same kind of table, but findFirst filters on revokedAt being null and on expiresAt being null or in the future, and a spent view budget returns 410, so the token stops working the moment it is revoked, expires or is used up.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: The file query parameter is joined onto ATTACHMENT_ROOT and the workspace directory and the result is read from disk with no normalisation and no containment check, so a value like ../../<other-workspace-id>/contract.pdf or ../../../../etc/passwd escapes the tenant directory even though the membership check on the document itself passed.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: The same shape - read a file whose name comes from a query parameter out of a directory built from an environment root - but the name is reduced with path.basename, resolved against the bundle directory, and rejected unless the resolved path still starts with that directory plus a separator; the directory segment itself comes from the export job row rather than the client.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: Every entry of the submitted FormData is coerced and copied into the patch object, which is then passed as Prisma's data argument for workspace.update, so a caller can post plan, seatLimit, retentionDays, ownerId or ssoRequired alongside the visible settings inputs and rewrite columns the settings form never exposes, including the billing tier and the seat entitlement.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
cases.why: inviteMember only requires that the caller hold some membership in the workspace and then writes the role taken from the form onto the invitation row; the only other gate is the seat count. A viewer can therefore invite a second address they control as owner and accept it to take full control of the workspace and its billing.

cases.architecture: Next.js 15 App Router application with route handlers under src/app/api and 'use server' action modules, Prisma Client 6 for data access, and the session read from a next-auth v5 auth() helper in src/lib/auth.ts.
